subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider `api_error: Internal server error` failures be classified for cron/fallback fast-fail and auth-profile cooldown behavior?
rationale: The same observed provider outage text can be modeled as `server_error`, `timeout`, or `overloaded`, and each choice changes whether cron retries, whether fallback exits early, and whether shared auth-profile health is cooled down.

options.title: Treat as transient server_error
options.body: Map plain provider internal-server text to a retryable server-outage reason for cron visibility and backoff without poisoning shared auth-profile health unless a narrower provider rule says otherwise.

options.title: Treat as overloaded cooldown
options.body: Adopt the #45625 direction and cool down affected provider/profile routes so repeated same-provider failures are skipped faster, accepting the wider provider-health semantics.

options.title: Defer to broader cron guardrails
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the wider reason-aware cron guardrail work and avoid changing provider classification until the full policy matrix is decided.

recommendation.title: Treat as transient server_error
recommendation.body: Map plain provider internal-server text to a retryable server-outage reason for cron visibility and backoff without poisoning shared auth-profile health unless a narrower provider rule says otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: altaywtf merged the structured `server_error` partial fix and is the strongest visible owner for the same failover/cron boundary.
